items.title: Trump claims Iran requested ceasefire; Tehran denies it

featured_image.name: CNBC Daily Open: Get ready for Trump's Iran war update

items.description:
President Donald Trump claimed on Wednesday that Iran's president had requested a ceasefire from the United States, posting the assertion on his Truth Social platform hours before a scheduled primetime address to the nation on the war in Iran. Trump conditioned any consideration of a pause in hostilities on Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the critical waterway through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil normally flows.

"The Iranian president has just requested a CEASEFIRE from the United States of America!" Trump wrote, according to DW News. "We will determine when the Strait of Hormuz is accessible and free. Until that time, we are relentlessly targeting Iran, or as they say, reverting them to the Stone Age!"[1]

items.title: Qubits needed to crack encryption fall 200-fold in under a year

featured_image.name: Breaking RSA encryption just got 20x easier for quantum computers | CSO  Online

items.description:
Three research papers published in the span of less than a year have dramatically reduced the estimated quantum computing resources needed to break modern encryption, compressing what many experts believed was a distant threat into a near-term challenge for governments, businesses, and the cryptocurrency industry.

The estimated number of physical qubits required to crack RSA-2048 encryption, the standard protecting most internet banking and digital certificates, has fallen from 20 million in 2019 to fewer than 100,000 under the latest architectures, according to a detailed analysis by The Quantum Insider published on Monday. In parallel, a Caltech and Oratomic team revealed on March 30 that fault-tolerant quantum computers could function with as few as 10,000 to 20,000 qubits, down from the millions previously thought necessary.[1][2]
